questions.key_step: Reject cases that make f not one-one; the surviving bijection gives f^-1(1).
questions.justification: Three short cases (or six bijections) on a tiny set; routine logic, no deep idea.

questions.key_step: P(x)-x has the six roots 1..6 and is monic of degree 6.
questions.justification: One familiar move (factor P(x)-x), then arithmetic.

questions.key_step: Odd part cancels, f(t)+f(-t)=8, and log10(log10 3) = -log10(log3 10).
questions.justification: Two short ideas chained: oddness plus the reciprocal-log identity; both familiar.
Single move: apply f^-1 and substitute; very direct.

questions.key_step: [x-1/2] = [x+1/2]-1, so the product of consecutive integers is prime only if 2; then convert to intervals.
questions.justification: Greatest-integer shift plus primality plus two interval cases and a final sum; each step is easy but a slip loses the answer.

questions.key_step: Remainder is linear and fixed by p(1) and p(4).
questions.justification: One standard result applied once.

questions.key_step: For x not an integer, ln of the second term equals -sqrt|ln{x}|, so both terms cancel and f is zero.
questions.justification: Needs the unfamiliar 'both even and odd means zero' insight and careful log manipulation with a fractional part; short once seen.

questions.key_step: The inner argument |sqrt2 sin(pi(x+1/4))| equals 1 at x = 1, 2, 1/2, giving three linear equations.
questions.justification: Spotting the special points and solving a linear system of three unknown values; more than routine but one idea.

questions.key_step: x=0 isolates f(y); x=y=1 gives k.
questions.justification: Standard functional-equation substitutions; routine chain of three.

questions.key_step: Collapse g-2 = -|x| for f o g; fold f in the axis for g o f; keep track of domains.
questions.justification: Four composites of modulus functions with domain restrictions and graphs: long, error-prone, but standard.

questions.key_step: Three substitutions (u=0; v=pi/2; u=pi/2) and the combination (1)+(3)-(2).
questions.justification: Choosing the right three substitutions and combining them is a genuine idea; routine afterwards.

questions.key_step: Onto means the quadratic in x has a real root for all y: discriminant is a non-negative quadratic in y.
questions.justification: Standard discriminant method for range, but with heavy algebra (factorising a quartic condition) and a second part about one-one.

questions.key_step: Count non-decreasing triples: cases by how many values coincide (or stars and bars).
questions.justification: One standard counting idea; short.

questions.key_step: Choose 3 range values (10) and count onto maps from 5 to 3 by inclusion-exclusion (150).
questions.justification: Needs onto-function counting formula and exact arithmetic with no options to check.

questions.key_step: The cos term is identically 0; the remaining terms have periods 4 and 1; classify 4.
questions.justification: Fractional-part periodicity with a hidden zero term; period of a sum needs care.
Quadratic inequality in [x] then interval conversion; routine, uses p from the previous part.
Short composition of a piecewise function; routine.

questions.key_step: Largest half-line where the parabola is one-one ends at the vertex (1,-2).
questions.justification: One familiar move: vertex of a parabola.

questions.key_step: g(|x|) has its minimum at x=0 because the vertex of g is at x=-1/2<0.
questions.justification: One short step after forming g; direct.

questions.key_step: Take the larger root since outputs of f^-1 lie in [1,inf).
questions.justification: Direct inverse of a quadratic on a restricted domain.

questions.key_step: f(|x|)=k has four roots iff t^2-2t-1-k=0 has two distinct positive roots (or W-shaped graph).
questions.justification: Standard modulus-graph / root-location reasoning; a few checks but routine.

questions.key_step: Four independent items: lcm of periods, shape of {sin pi x}, sign pattern of a modulus expression, endpoint mapping of a bijection.
questions.justification: Item C needs a careful quadrant analysis to get the fundamental period 8, and A/B have two matches each; four separate checks.

questions.key_step: Domain emptiness in A, bound LHS<2<=RHS in B, empty intersection in C, common domain in D.
questions.justification: Four short standard checks; B needs a small bound but the rest is direct.

questions.key_step: Evaluate each part to a number (1, 2, 3) and classify; inverse of a Mobius map; composition identity; iterated linear map.
